details: A modified fork of the WhatsApp "Baileys" library that covertly enrols the connected WhatsApp account into four hardcoded channels. The package inserts code into the makeNewsletterSocket() factory in lib/Socket/newsletter.js: when a client connects, two 90-second timers (each followed by a second query after 5 seconds) decode four base64 string literals and send them as WhatsApp newsletter FOLLOW queries over the encrypted socket (xmpp xmlns "w:mex", query id Types.QueryIds.FOLLOW). The base64 encoding hides the channel identifiers from review, the 90-second delay places the action outside a short inspection window, and the calls are wrapped in empty try/catch blocks with their responses discarded so nothing is logged or surfaced to the application. The four decoded channel JIDs are 120363400706010828@newsletter, 120363423257544642@newsletter, 120363349457176430@newsletter and 120363421052027188@newsletter. Any application built on this library silently force-follows these channels for its own account without requesting or reporting it. No other network destination, credential access or file collection was found in the tree; the only additional remote reference is a version-metadata JSON fetched from raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/kiuur/bails.
